notes: Sky-sign/eminent-domain police-power case (advertising structure ordinance); no bearing on letting of dwellings or lodging/boarding regulation.
Fire-insurance forfeiture case turning on vacancy/occupancy of owner's own dwelling; not about compensated letting to lodgers/boarders.
Covenant-running-with-the-land / light-and-air easement dispute; mentions the building was later used 'as a hotel' only incidentally to the covenant analysis, not addressing letting practice.
Innkeeper tort/slander liability for an employee's insult to a hotel guest; addresses scope of innkeeper's implied contract of protection, not the legal character or regulation of letting rooms.
Sidewalk-grating personal-injury case; the matched text ('let rooms, and did repairs') is a passing description of a building manager's duties, not a holding about letting practice.

Landlord premises-liability case construing the statutory definition of 'tenement house' (three families with common right to halls/stairs/yard) for purposes of the hallway-lighting statute; concerns ordinary multi-family tenancy, not compensated short-term letting or boarding/lodging characterization.

Police-power case sustaining sanitary/plumbing requirements (removal of school sinks) in a multi-family tenement house; regulates building sanitation generally, not the letting of rooms/dwellings for pay or licensing of lodging/boarding houses specifically.
Garbage-transportation licensing ordinance struck down as an invalid delegation of arbitrary permit power; no relation to letting or lodging of dwellings.

holding_summary: A landlord sought summary dispossession of a tenant who leased premises to be used as a boarding house, on the theory that the premises were being run as a disorderly house. The court found the police officers' testimony (women reading in ordinary dress, no evidence of immoral conduct observed on the premises) insufficient to establish an unlawful use, and reversed the order removing the tenant.

quotes.text: The tenant herein was a lessee of premises ; the lease providing that it should be used and occupied as a boarding house, and for no other purpose.

The evidence fails to show that the defendant kept a house prohibited by law. The mere fact that an immoral woman lives in a house, or visits one, is not sufficient to show that the tenant keeps a bawdy house.
The granting of the order herein was clearly against the weight of evidence, and must be reversed.

holding_summary: Plaintiff's assignor, at the request of the defendant's testator, leased a summer cottage and agreed to furnish the testator and his family with board, service, and general care at $100 per week for a five-month period (June 1 to November 1, 1900). After the testator died mid-term and his family moved out, the court held it was a fair jury question whether the parties intended the boarding arrangement to bind the family for the whole five-month period, reversing for a new trial (though also on an evidentiary error).

quotes.text: by which it was agreed that the latter was to pay $ioo per week for the exclusive possession and use of said Beatty Cottage, and stables and premises, for the said period from June 1st to November 1st, 1900, upon condition that the plaintiff's assignor would provide the service and board and have the general care of the said premises during the said period.

I think it was a fair question for the jury, from the circumstances proved by the plaintiff, whether there was an obligation to occupy the premises under the agreement, and that such occupation was to be for the whole period, from the ist of June to the ist of November.

It could not be assumed to have been within the contemplation of the parties that where a person had thus, at the Instigation of another, leased a house for a particular period, with the understanding that the whole house should be reserved for the suse of the party at whose instigation it was leased, such party could terminate the contract at any time

notes: Ejectment case about mortgagee-in-possession rights following a life tenant's lease; concerns title/possession priority among mortgagee, reversioner, and lessee, not the character or regulation of lodging/boarding arrangements.
Bakery labor-hours statute (Lochner-line) sustained as police-power regulation of employment; no relation to letting of dwellings or lodging-house regulation.

Summary-proceeding case holding that an informal family arrangement (mother's house owner; daughter and son-in-law to live there, board the mother, and keep the house in repair 'during her pleasure') did not create a landlord-tenant relationship for eviction purposes. This is a family support arrangement without rent or a stranger-lodger, not a compensated letting or boarding-house transaction; not counted as bearing on the corpus's core practice, though doctrinally adjacent to license/tenancy line-drawing.
Municipal sidewalk-encroachment nuisance case (bank building columns); no relation to letting or lodging.

Dispute over return of an earnest-money deposit for the sale of the 'contents and good will of a furnished room house' business; the holding concerns escrow/conversion proof, not the legal character or regulation of letting furnished rooms.
Ordinary commercial lease holding-over case (subtenant's involuntary holdover binds original tenant for another term); no lodging/boarding subject matter.
Saloon lease holding-over/chattel-mortgage dispute; no relation to dwelling letting or lodging.
Commercial lease-renewal option dispute (meat-packing business premises); no lodging/boarding subject matter.
